title: Somalia Three-Vessel Piracy Crisis Day 29/28/22 — 44 Hostages as Iran War Continues to Deplete Counter-Piracy Naval Capacity; No Rescue Timeline
detail: Somalia's unprecedented three-vessel piracy hostage crisis continued on May 24, 2026: Honour 25 (Day 29), Sward (Day 28), and MT Eureka (Day 22) remained under pirate control with all 44 hostages captive and no ransom payments or rescue operations reported as of May 24. The situation continued to deteriorate for Honour 25 crew families, who had repeatedly appealed publicly for government intervention since the vessel was seized off Puntland on April 25. The crew — 10 Pakistanis, 4 Indonesians, 1 Indian, 1 Sri Lankan, and 1 Myanmar national — remained confined aboard with critical living conditions: one daily rice serving, no clean water, and medicine exhausted. Pakistan's Foreign Ministry maintained its no-ransom policy while international naval assets remained diverted. EU NAVFOR Atalanta and Combined Task Force 151 counter-piracy patrol capacity continued to be drawn down by the demands of the Iran War in the Persian Gulf and Red Sea, leaving the Gulf of Aden and northwestern Indian Ocean with significantly reduced military deterrence. The Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) had confirmed on May 14 that Iran-backed Houthis were providing weapons and GPS tracking devices to Somali pirates — a nexus documented by the Puntland Maritime Police Force and an October 2025 UN Panel of Experts report on Yemen — adding an Iran War geopolitical dimension to what had previously been characterized as a criminal opportunity. The JMIC 'severe' threat level remained in force. No mechanism for parallel rescue had emerged from Kenya, Djibouti, or regional partners. Al Jazeera estimated that the three-vessel crisis had generated the worst hostage situation in the western Indian Ocean since the peak Somali piracy era of 2010–2012.

media.caption: Al Jazeera: Fear grips Pakistani families of Somali piracy victims — Honour 25 and two other vessels enter Day 29/28/22 with no rescue timeline

title: Adan Yabal Day 35 Under Al-Shabaab; Somalia Opposition Parallel-Authority Countdown Day 9 — CFR, Addis Standard Track Somalia's Constitutional Void as Security Deteriorates
detail: Somalia's twin political-security crisis extended through May 24, 2026: Al-Shabaab continued to hold Adan Yabal in Hiiraan Region for Day 35 — the longest uncontested insurgent occupation of a Hiiraan town since the 2022 SNA/Macawisley offensive — while the opposition Somali Future Council's deadline countdown to establishing a parallel transitional authority entered Day 9. President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud's government, operating under disputed March 2026 constitutional amendments rejected by Puntland, Jubbaland, and the Somali Future Council, faced growing domestic and international pressure as the constitutional deadlock showed no signs of resolution. CFR's Global Conflict Tracker identified Somalia's political paralysis as severely hampering the anti-Al-Shabaab war effort, with analysts noting that the SNA's operational command remained distracted by Mogadishu's constitutional dispute. The Addis Standard characterized the situation as 'Mandate Expired, Authority Retained,' noting that Somalia's term-limit crisis and the collapse of the Halane talks had left the country without a legitimately agreed political framework. AUSSOM forces (authorized at ~12,626 troops under UNSC Resolution 2809) remained in a capital protective posture rather than projecting power to Hiiraan or other contested regions. Macawisley clan militia cohesion — the backbone of the 2022 anti-Al-Shabaab offensive in Hiiraan — continued to weaken without federal political and logistical backing. Al-Shabaab had used the 35-day period to reinforce Adan Yabal's defensive positions and consolidate shadow governance in adjacent areas. ACLED data showed Hiiraan conflict events at their highest monthly pace since September 2022. The humanitarian dimension compounded the security deterioration: FEWS NET's Burhakaba famine-risk alert (Bay Region, 37.1% GAM) and WFP's July 2026 operational shutdown warning remained active, with only 13.4% of the $852 million Humanitarian Response Plan funded.

media.caption: Addis Standard: Somalia opposition-government talks amid deepening constitutional crisis — Day 9 of opposition countdown as Adan Yabal enters Day 35 under Al-Shabaab
